strategy.summary: Reproduce NumPy special-value sorting bug (complex NaN ordering) from numpy/numpy#31572 by running the core multiarray test that validates descending complex sort semantics when real-part NaNs must be the primary key. The test should fail on buggy commit b1b77568be65 and pass on the fixed revision.

strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_multiarray.py::test_sort_descending_complex_lexorder (or the parameterized variant covering descending complex lexicographic ordering; selected by -k "sort_descending_complex")
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (commit b1b77568be65), the descending sort test for complex values fails because complex numbers with only imaginary NaNs are incorrectly ordered before those with only real NaNs; on the fixed revision from PR #31572, the same test passes because real NaNs are ordered as the primary key in descending order (so real-only-NaN complex values sort after imaginary-only-NaN complex values).
strategy.numerical_probe: The test relies on constructing complex arrays with NaNs in real-only, imaginary-only, and both parts, then asserting the relative ordering produced by the descending complex sort (no direct numeric tolerances; ordering against NaN masks is the oracle).

input_output_examples.input: Sort complex values in descending order with two elements: one complex with real NaN only and one with imaginary NaN only.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Imaginary-only-NaN complex values come before real-only-NaN complex values in descending order.
input_output_examples.expected_output: Real-only-NaN complex values come after imaginary-only-NaN complex values in descending order (real NaNs are the primary key).
